title: On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying and synthesizing literature on representational biases, modified implicit association tests for models, and performance disparities in downstream applications such as speech recognition for African American English, facial recognition for darker skin tones, and clinical notes.

Surveying literature on representational harms, including default male pronoun misgendering in machine translation, modified implicit association tests, and performance disparities in clinical natural language processing.
Discussing literature on the generation of pernicious stereotypes and persistent anti-Muslim bias in large language models.

Examining performance disparities on non-standard dialects (e.g., African American English) and evaluating implicit Anglocentric perspectives or similarity metrics encoded by default in models like BERT.
Reviewing literature that identifies undesirable biases and representational harms towards disabled persons within foundation models.
Discussing representational bias through the underrepresentation or complete erasure of LGBTQ+ identity terms in training data and subsequent model behavior.
Reviewing performance disparities and incorrect medical condition detections from clinical notes for minority groups based on insurance-status.
